item.title: Traditional rice wine brewing boosts local economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Winemaker Zhan Rongbin seals the rice wine in jars for fermentation in Kengtou Village of Wuyuan County, east China's Jiangxi Province, Nov. 24, 2026. Leveraging its history and culture of wine-making, Kengtou Village in Wuyuan County of Shangrao City has actively promoted the development of the rice wine industry in recent years, creating job opportunities for local villagers. The village produces about 250,000 kilograms of rice wine annually, with an output value exceeding six million yuan (about 0.9 million U.S. dollars). In 2020, the Kengtou rice wine brewing technique was included in the fifth batch of the municipal intangible cultural heritage list for representative items of Shangrao City. item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani payload specialist, to its orbiting Tiangong space station. The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The astronauts aboard the spaceship are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first-ever foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. The Shenzhou-24 mission marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. ■ The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. item.title: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China has spearheaded the development of 78 international standards on artificial intelligence (AI), turning its industrial practices and technological innovations into global public goods, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Sun Wei, deputy head of the department of standards innovation under the SAMR, told a press conference Tuesday that the body has made active efforts to help improve the international standards system architecture for AI. Working with leading companies and top research institutions, the SAMR has led the development of 29 foundational and common international standards, covering key areas that include data governance, human-computer interaction, security and trustworthiness, Sun said. In addition, the SAMR has coordinated the efforts of 15 technical standards bodies in developing 49 international standards for sector-specific applications, including smart cities and intelligent manufacturing, according to the official. Sectoral application standards act as a key lever to drive the scaled and standardized implementation of AI technologies. In recent years, the SAMR has expanded its efforts to advance international standards in key areas, such as smart manufacturing, smart cities, smart logistics and smart water management, drawing on China's extensive application scenarios and mature industrial practices. Sun said China's systematic efforts to develop application-oriented standards across multiple industries offered technical standards and practical solutions for wider international adoption, supporting AI-empowered real economy development and inclusive, shared digital transformation. The SAMR also revealed that, in response to common risks such as deepfakes and model "poisoning" in generative AI, China has jointly developed with multiple countries a guideline on addressing risks in generative AI. According to the SAMR, this marked the world's first international standards proposal targeting generative AI governance and can provide key support for promoting the formation of a global consensus on risk management. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: China's space station opens a new chapter in int'l cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-24 mission marks a milestone in China's manned space program as a Pakistani astronaut becomes the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station, opening a new chapter in China's efforts to advance international cooperation in space exploration. Over the years, China has built its space station through independent innovation and technological development, demonstrating its growing capabilities in manned spaceflight. Its experience shows that self-reliance and international cooperation are not mutually exclusive. While independent development has laid a solid foundation for China's space program, openness is creating new opportunities for its continued progress. China has increasingly sought to make its space program more accessible to international partners, offering opportunities for other countries to participate in scientific research and space exploration. The Shenzhou-24 mission is a concrete step in this direction. For Pakistan, the mission offers an opportunity to develop expertise in human spaceflight, strengthen its astronaut training capabilities and participate in scientific experiments in orbit. For China, it marks the first joint spaceflight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts, extending bilateral cooperation into a new frontier. The experience could also pave the way for broader international participation in China's space program. Space exploration transcends national borders and offers opportunities for countries to advance scientific knowledge through cooperation. China has consistently advocated the peaceful use of outer space and promoted international collaboration in this field. A case in point is China's recent donation to the United Nations of a lunar soil sample collected by the Chang'e-6 mission from the far side of the Moon. By sharing the fruits of its space exploration with the international community, China is helping create opportunities for joint research and enabling more countries to benefit from advances in space science. Space exploration should not be an exclusive endeavor, but a shared undertaking that brings countries together through the exchange of knowledge, technology and talent. By opening its space station to international partners, China is creating opportunities for scientific collaboration and contributing to the peaceful use of outer space.■

item.title: Launch of Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship a complete success: CMSA
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Wednesday that the launch of the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship was "a complete success." The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, sending Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to China's orbiting Tiangong space station, according to the CMSA. About 10 minutes after the launch, the spaceship separated from the rocket and entered its designated orbit, the CMSA said, adding that the astronauts are in good condition. ■

Guo Yandong poses for photos with a robot at Ai² Robotics in Nanshan District of Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 12, 2026. During the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, seven AlphaBot robots stationed at the media center provided services for Chinese and foreign journalists, operating reliably and serving drinks over seven consecutive days. These robots are from Ai² Robotics, a robotics startup founded in early 2023 in Shenzhen by Guo Yandong. Guo believes that humanoid robots must be deployed in real scenarios for practical assignments. With this end goal in mind, he has oriented Ai² Robotics toward developing productivity-focused intelligent robots. The AlphaBot robots are now in service across Shenzhen for airport, industrial, urban governance and emergency-response tasks. Guo's vision of robots as the fourth-generation intelligent terminals following personal computers, mobile phones and smart vehicles is steadily taking shape. item.title: China ranks among global leaders in 6G patent applications
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
SHANGHAI, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- China is among the world's top countries in 6G patent applications and has developed more than 300 key 6G technology assets, according to the 2026 Global 6G Development Conference held in Shanghai on Tuesday. "Our 5G networks have been operating for years, laying a solid foundation for 6G evolution, and this foundation has also benefited from cooperation across the global industry," said Wen Ku, chairman of the China Communications Standards Association. As of the end of August, China had built about 5.19 million 5G base stations. From 3G to 5G, globally unified standards have delivered economies of scale that significantly lowered the cost of communications equipment and connected billions of people to the digital world, and 6G should continue on the path of cooperative development, Wen said. Zhong Zhihong, chief engineer of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, said 6G technology is now at a critical stage of deepening technological breakthroughs and advancing comprehensive standards development, making it all the more necessary for global industry, academia and research parties to build consensus and cooperate closely. At the conference, the IMT-2030 (6G) promotion group, together with major international organizations, industry alliances and leading Chinese and international enterprises, released the Global 6G Development Philosophy Declaration. The declaration sets out five concepts, including cross-domain integrated innovation with intrinsic intelligence at its core, green and sustainable development throughout the entire chain, and a secure and trustworthy system based on all-domain security, among others. The conference also launched a pilot program for 6G innovative development jointly by the ministry and provincial governments. Eight provincial-level regions, namely Beijing, Hebei in north China, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui in east China, Hubei in central China and Guangdong in south China, are participating to jointly build a coordinated national framework for 6G innovation. ■

item.title: Xi Story: Vision over a century old meets a changing China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
BEIJING, Nov. 24 (Xinhua) -- Dr. Sun Yat-sen once envisioned an ambitious blueprint for China's modernization in a landmark work compiled from his writings finished between 1917 and 1919, featuring plans for an extensive railway and road network as well as world-class ports. "Many of the goals Dr. Sun Yat-sen set forth have been realized, and what we have accomplished has gone far beyond anything he could have imagined," President Xi Jinping said last week at a museum in honor of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, in south China's Guangdong Province. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Upon arrival at the museum located in the city of Zhongshan, Sun's hometown, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, laid a floral basket before the pioneer's bronze statue and bowed in tribute. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Earlier in November, Xi addressed a gathering held in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to mark Sun's 160th birth anniversary, hailing Sun as "a great national hero, a great patriot, and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution." At the gathering, Xi highlighted Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, noting that Sun's call for "revitalizing China" has inspired generation after generation of Chinese, taking on renewed significance with each passing era. The president called for carrying forward Sun's legacy, working together to advance national rejuvenation, and turning into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi's visit to the museum, part of an inspection tour in Zhongshan on Nov. 16, offered a glimpse of how Sun's vision of a strong and prosperous China has taken shape today. Sun once envisioned developing the country around three great ports -- in the north, the east and the south. The three powerhouses of China's economy today, the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, echo Sun's original design, Xi noted at the museum. "Dr. Sun's national railway map envisaged 160,000 kilometers," Xi said, noting that China's railway network has since surpassed that figure. By the end of 2025, the country's railway network had spanned 165,000 kilometers in total, including 50,000 kilometers of operational high-speed railway, which accounted for 70 percent of the world's total. "Today, the Chinese economy ranks second in the world. Chinese people have achieved moderate prosperity in all respects, and the Chinese nation has stood up, grown rich and become strong," Xi said. China is also continuing to make new contributions to the development and progress of human society, he added. This transformation Sun once dreamed of is also evident in his hometown and the surrounding area. Before visiting the museum, Xi inspected the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a mega cross-sea passage connecting cities on opposite sides of the Pearl River Estuary. The link cuts travel time between the technology hub of Shenzhen and the manufacturing city of Zhongshan from about two hours to roughly 30 minutes, facilitating integration across the Greater Bay Area. Over the years, Xi has made several inspection tours of the Greater Bay Area. Sun's former residence and the museum exhibition hall in Zhongshan are just a short distance apart. "I have been here before, but this visit has given me new impressions," Xi said. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered an irreversible historical process," Xi said, calling for sustained efforts to advance the great cause. ■
